meta.parties: Wadurala v. The Sunderland Rubber Co

rules.statement: Where damage is part of the cause of action, and no act is committed which is of itself wrongful, the statute of limitations runs from the date of the damage, and not of the act which causes the damage.
rules.supporting_quote: "The authorities cited do not support that view at all. The passage from Halsbury's Laws of England, vol. XIX., p. 52, shows that when damage is part of the cause of action, and no act is committed which is of itself wrongful, the statute of limitations runs from the date of the damage, and not of the act which causes the damage." (Pereira J.)
